REVERSE() and SUBSTRING() of an integer argument return the result converted back to the argument's integer type (REVERSE(127) on a TINYINT is 127, MySQL returns '721'; SUBSTRING(105, 2) is 5, MySQL returns '05')
UNION of a DECIMAL and a DOUBLE returns 0.000000000000000000000000000000 for large DOUBLE values (SELECT 1.5 UNION SELECT 1.7e308 returns 1.5 and 0.000...)
UNION of a signed and an unsigned integer returns values above 9223372036854775807 as negative numbers (SELECT 1 UNION SELECT 18446744073709551615 returns 1 and -1)

Computed DOUBLE values are returned in exponent notation from 1e6 up and for 1e-5 (SELECT 1e6 is '1e+06', d + 0 for 1234567.5 is '1.2345675e+06', SUM(d) is '1.0000001357913562e+15'); MySQL returns 1000000, 1234567.5 and 1000000135791356.2
LEFT() and RIGHT() with an integer first argument fail with ERROR 1105 "invalid type: int8" (MySQL converts the number to a string: LEFT(105, 2) is '10')
CAST(x AS DECIMAL(p,s)) returns 0 when the value does not fit into the type; MySQL returns the largest value that fits (CAST(100000000 AS DECIMAL(10,2)) is 99999999.99)
FORMAT(x, d) returns 0.00 for every value of 2^63 or more (BIGINT UNSIGNED, DECIMAL, DOUBLE, literals) and rounds integers above 2^53 through a double

Signed arithmetic with an integer literal of 128..255, 32768..65535 or 2147483648..4294967295 fails with ERROR 1690 "BIGINT UNSIGNED value is out of range" when the result is negative (works in 2.3.3, fails since 2.3.4)
WITH RECURSIVE with ORDER BY over the UNION inside the CTE fails with "unable to sort: unable to find field with index 2 in row of 1 columns. This is a bug."
Unary minus and MOD on a DATE or DATETIME value give wrong numbers: -d is -2.0200229e+13 (MySQL -20200229), d MOD 100 is 0 (MySQL 29), dt MOD 100 is 0 (MySQL 56), -dt has wrong digits
A TIME value used as a number is 0 (t + 0, t * 1, -t, t MOD 100, CAST(t AS SIGNED)) and ABS(t) fails with "'types.Timespan' is not a valid value type for 'double'"; MySQL returns HHMMSS (123456)
DATE'...', TIME'...' and TIMESTAMP'...' literals used as numbers give only their leading digits (DATE'2020-02-29' + 0 is 2020, TIME'12:34:56' + 0 is 12); MySQL gives 20200229 and 123456

A DATE value is converted to text in DATETIME form by string functions: CONCAT(s, date_col) is 'x2020-02-29 00:00:00', LENGTH(date_col) is 19, LEFT() and RIGHT() fail with "invalid type: time.Time", REVERSE() and SUBSTRING() fail with ERROR 1525

Comparing an integer with a DATE or DATETIME value gives different results from MySQL: 20200228 < DATE'2020-02-29' is 0 (MySQL 1), WHERE int_col < date_col drops rows, and the literal and column forms disagree
TIME_TO_SEC() of a negative time returns an unsigned 64-bit wrap-around value (TIME_TO_SEC('-00:00:05') is 18446744073709551611, MySQL returns -5)
VARBINARY, BINARY and BLOB values are read as big-endian integers in arithmetic, comparisons, SUM() and CAST(... AS SIGNED) (MySQL parses the text: '12' + 1 is 13, Dolt returns 12595)
